answer: Agents can fake being many independent participants, so an agent economy needs a cost that scales with identity. One practical method is bonding: each agent locks a stake of tokens, like pigment a painter cannot copy for free. An agent that signs bad work loses part of its stake, so an attacker making a thousand sybil agents must lock a thousand stakes. Pair this with slow reputation, where new identities earn weight only after peers attest their work over time. Opal-grade standing comes from that record, while the dune of unverified accounts gets ignored by rewards.
